spots.name: Doughmore
spots.hazards: DANGEROUS RIP CURRENTS — strong rips pull out across this bay and are the main hazard here; know your exits before paddling out. Exposed flat rocks at low tide on the reef side (left/north end) can cause impacts on closeouts. Big open beach: conditions and currents vary along its length.
spots.notes: Large, open beach — effectively two spots. The main sandy beach (what you'll normally surf) is a forgiving beach break working rights and lefts across all tides. There is ALSO a powerful left-hand reef over flat rocks to the LEFT (north) of the beach: that reef is advanced-only, needs 1.5 m+, and is best mid-high when the rocks are covered — it does NOT work all tides like the beach does. Very consistent year-round; best Oct-Mar. Rarely crowded.

spots.name: Lahinch
spots.hazards: Rips on bigger swells; scattered rocks at the headland ends.
spots.notes: Pure beach break, rights and lefts, punchy A-frames on clean days. Low-mid tide gives the best shape. Peaks Sep-Mar. Often crowded but the beach is long enough to spread out.

spots.name: Fanore
spots.hazards: Rocks exposed at low tide; rips on bigger swells; summer jellyfish.
spots.notes: Beginner-friendly beach break over sand with some rock, rights and lefts. Mid tide is ideal. Decent consistency on NW swell; often empty midweek. Burren scenery.

spots.name: White Strand
spots.hazards: Rips and undertow over 1.5 m; rocks exposed at low tide.
spots.notes: Sheltered beach break (aka Killard), rights and lefts, mellow A-frames. HIGH tide only and best on a rising tide — it covers the rocks and makes the wave. Best Oct-Mar; usually empty.

spots.name: Easkey Left
spots.hazards: Rocks in the take-off zone; rip off the pier on bigger swells. Boulder bottom — booties recommended.
spots.notes: Left-hand reef over boulders; hollow, fast, can barrel. Works all tides, low tide sharpens the take-off over the rocks. Peaks Dec-Feb on NW groundswell with S offshore.

spots.name: Easkey Right
spots.hazards: Sharp reef and rocks — precision needed. Avoid above ~1.8 m unless very experienced. Rivermouth rip pushes off the peak.
spots.notes: Powerful right-hand point over sharp reef; long walls, hollow when firing. LOW tide only for the cleanest shape. Use the rivermouth rip to get out. Remarkably consistent; best Nov-Mar.

spots.name: Strandhill
spots.hazards: Strong rips; rocks at low tide or after winter erosion. High tide can cut off access near the promenade.
spots.notes: Very consistent beach/sandbar break (~150 days/yr), rights and lefts off shifting banks. Mid-high tide is prime — low gets shorey and rocky. Best when swell stays under 2 m.

spots.name: Bertra
spots.notes: Sheltered Clew Bay sand beach; needs bigger swell. Orientation INFERRED from The Magharees (similar exposed sand beach) — no direct data gathered.

spots.name: Keel
spots.hazards: Rips on bigger SW swells; exposed rocks at low tide.
spots.notes: Achill Island beach break over sand, lefts and rights, fun A-frames. Mid-high tide when the sandbars peak. Best Sep-Mar on SW swell with E/NE offshore. Quiet midweek.

spots.name: The Magharees
spots.hazards: Rips in bigger surf across the wide beach; no major rocks.
spots.notes: Brandon Bay / Maharees: long sandy beach break with multiple peaks, lefts and rights. Works all tides — very flexible. Mellow and forgiving; best Sep-Apr. Rarely crowded.
